M O B I L E S Y S T E M
E D I T I O N · M I D - L E V E L I N T E R V I E W
JavaScript.
React. TypeScript.
Systems. AI.
A phone-first field manual for becoming the
engineer who can explain what something
is, why it exists, how it behaves in code,
and where it breaks.
310
CONCEPT CARDS
1 : 1
CONCEPT PER PAGE
16
MENTAL MODELS
12
SYSTEM DRILLS

START
H OW TO U S E T H I S O N YO U R P H O N E
No zoom. No glossary
wall. One mental model
at a time.
1 · Read “IN ONE BREATH”
If you cannot explain the definition in one breath, reread it.
2 · Read the ridiculous memory hook
Silly is deliberate. Weird images are easier for your brain
to retrieve under interview pressure.
3 · Predict the real example
Before reading the explanation, ask what the code/system
will do and why.
4 · Say the interview answer aloud
Do not memorize it word-for-word. Keep the structure:
definition → purpose → example → trade-off.
5 · Name one failure mode
That final trade-off is what often makes an answer sound
mid-level instead of junior.

The mid-level answer
engine
1. WHAT?
Give a clean definition with the correct noun. “A CDN is a
geographically distributed delivery/cache layer...”
2. WHY?
Name the engineering pressure it solves: latency,
correctness, maintainability, concurrency, cost, security...
3. EXAMPLE?
Make it concrete in ordinary product code. Browser → API
→ cache → database beats abstract vocabulary.
4. TRADE-OFF?
Say what it costs or when you would not use it. Mid-level
engineers know tools create new problems too.
5. FAILURE MODE?
Show that you can operate software, not just design happy
paths: stale cache, race, retry storm, leaked secret, slow
query...

MAP
T H E L E A R N I N G R OA D M A P
Start with the web. End
with AI systems.
Study in order once. After that, jump by section based
on interview weakness.
01 WEB, NETWORKING & DELIVERY
How browser requests travel, get routed, cached, and returned.
02 SECURITY, IDENTITY & TRUST
Who you are, what you may do, and how systems defend the
path.
03 DATABASES & DATA INTEGRITY
How persistent data stays related, correct, and fast under
concurrency.
04 REALTIME & ASYNC JAVASCRIPT
How apps wait, stream, schedule, and react without freezing.
05 JAVASCRIPT CORE MENTAL MODELS
The language behaviors behind most interview gotchas.
06 TYPESCRIPT & REACT FOUNDATIONS
Types, components, state, effects, identity, and reuse.
07 FRONTEND PLATFORM, UX & PERFORMANCE
Rendering, accessibility, loading, navigation, and perceived
speed.

MAP
T H E L E A R N I N G R OA D M A P
Continue the map.
Study in order once. After that, jump by section based
on interview weakness.
08 RELIABILITY, ARCHITECTURE & DELIVERY
Failure handling, queues, deployment, observability, and system
shape.
09 COMPUTER SCIENCE & ENGINEERING JUDGMENT
Data structures, complexity, memory, purity, and pragmatic
principles.
10 TYPESCRIPT: THINKING IN TYPES
Move from “TypeScript syntax” to modeling states and contracts
so invalid code is harder to write.
11 REACT: STATE, IDENTITY & ARCHITECTURE
How to build React interfaces that stay predictable as features,
async work, and teams grow.
12 MODULARITY & MAINTAINABILITY
How to make change cheap: clear boundaries, contracts,
dependencies, and refactoring discipline.
13 DATABASES IN PRODUCTION
Beyond CRUD: schema design, constraints, concurrency, query
plans, migrations, and scale.
14 CACHING, PERFORMANCE & SCALABILITY
How systems stay fast under load without serving stale
nonsense or collapsing when dependencies slow down.

MAP
T H E L E A R N I N G R OA D M A P
Continue the map.
Study in order once. After that, jump by section based
on interview weakness.
15 AI ENGINEERING & LLM SYSTEMS
The practical vocabulary behind modern AI products: tokens,
retrieval, inference, caching, agents, safety, and evaluation.
16 TESTING, SECURITY & OPERATIONAL EXCELLENCE
The practices that keep a correct-looking app trustworthy after
real users, deploys, attackers, and failures arrive.

S E C T I O N 0 1
Web, Networking &
Delivery
How browser requests travel, get routed,
cached, and returned.
Database

Browser DNS

001
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
HTTP
I N O N E B R E AT H
The request-response protocol used by browsers,
apps, and servers to exchange web data. It is the basic
language behind APIs, pages, images, and most web
traffic.
M A K E I T S T I C K
HTTP is a waiter: you order GET /pizza; the kitchen
sends a response.
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /users/42 -> 200 + JSON user data.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
HTTP is a stateless request-response protocol. I use
methods, headers, status codes, and bodies to define
the contract between client and server.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 001 / 310

002
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
HTTPS
I N O N E B R E AT H
HTTP carried through TLS so traffic is encrypted and
the server can prove its identity. It protects credentials,
tokens, and user data from easy interception or
tampering.
M A K E I T S T I C K
HTTP is shouting your password across a cafe.
HTTPS is whispering through a locked tube.
R E A L E X A M P L E
https://example.com/login encrypts the request
while it travels over the network.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
HTTPS is HTTP over TLS. TLS gives confidentiality,
integrity, and server authentication.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 002 / 310

003
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
TLS
I N O N E B R E AT H
A security protocol that establishes an encrypted,
integrity-protected connection between peers. It is
what makes HTTPS trustworthy in transit.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Two spies agree on a secret code, then talk where
everyone can hear but nobody can understand.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Browser verifies a certificate, negotiates keys,
then sends encrypted HTTP.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
TLS provides encryption, integrity, and authentication
for network connections; HTTPS uses TLS underneath.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 003 / 310

004
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
DNS
I N O N E B R E AT H
The naming system that translates human-friendly
domains into network addresses. Users remember
example.com, not server IP addresses.
M A K E I T S T I C K
DNS is your phone contacts: tap "Mum" instead of
memorizing her number.
R E A L E X A M P L E
api.example.com -> an IP address returned by a
DNS resolver.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
DNS maps names to records such as IP addresses so
clients can locate services.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 004 / 310

005
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
IP address
I N O N E B R E AT H
A network address used to identify where packets
should be delivered. Networking needs an addressable
destination for hosts and interfaces.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The IP is the apartment building address; you still
need the port to find the right door.
R E A L E X A M P L E
192.168.1.20 is a private IPv4 address; IPv6
uses a larger address space.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An IP address identifies a network endpoint.
Applications usually reach it indirectly through DNS.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 005 / 310

006
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Port
I N O N E B R E AT H
A numeric identifier that distinguishes services on the
same host. One machine can run a web app, database,
cache, and more at the same IP.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Same apartment building, different doorbells: 3000
for the app, 5432 for Postgres.
R E A L E X A M P L E
localhost:5173 and localhost:8000 reach
different processes on the same computer.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A port selects the service or process at a host address;
the combination of protocol, host, and port helps identify
an endpoint.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 006 / 310

007
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Request
I N O N E B R E AT H
A message a client sends asking a server to perform
an operation or return data. It carries the method, URL,
headers, and sometimes a body.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You hand the barista a card saying: POST coffee, oat
milk, extra hot.
R E A L E X A M P L E
POST /users with Content-Type: application/json
and a JSON body.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An HTTP request contains a method, target URL,
headers, and optionally a body.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 007 / 310

008
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Response
I N O N E B R E AT H
The server message that reports the result of a
request. It communicates success or failure plus
headers and optional content.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The kitchen hands back your meal plus a receipt
saying 200 OK.
R E A L E X A M P L E
201 Created with a new resource representation
after POST /users.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An HTTP response includes a status code, headers, and
usually a body describing the result.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 008 / 310

009
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
HTTP methods
I N O N E B R E AT H
Standard verbs that express what operation a request
intends to perform. They make API contracts
predictable and communicate semantics to clients,
caches, and infrastructure.
M A K E I T S T I C K
GET looks, POST creates, PATCH edits, DELETE
throws it in the bin.
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /users reads; POST /users creates; PATCH /
users/42 updates part; DELETE removes.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use HTTP methods according to their semantics: GET
for retrieval, POST for creation/actions, PUT for
replacement, PATCH for partial updates, DELETE for
removal.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 009 / 310

010
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
HTTP status codes
I N O N E B R E AT H
Three-digit codes that summarize the outcome of an
HTTP response. They let clients handle success,
redirects, client errors, and server errors consistently.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A restaurant scorecard: 2xx "here is dinner", 4xx
"you ordered nonsense", 5xx "the kitchen is on fire".
R E A L E X A M P L E
200 OK, 201 Created, 204 No Content, 400 Bad
Request, 401, 403, 404, 409, 429, 500, 503.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I treat 2xx as success, 4xx as client-side request/auth
issues, and 5xx as server-side failures; specific codes
matter for client behavior.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 010 / 310

011
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Headers
I N O N E B R E AT H
Metadata fields attached to HTTP requests and
responses. They carry information such as content
type, authorization, caching rules, and tracing IDs.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The parcel label is not the gift; it says what is inside
and where it should go.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Authorization: Bearer ..., Content-Type:
application/json, Cache-Control: max-age=3600.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Headers carry protocol metadata separate from the
main payload, for example auth, caching, content
negotiation, and correlation IDs.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 011 / 310

012
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Request body
I N O N E B R E AT H
The payload sent inside a request, commonly with
POST, PUT, or PATCH. It transports structured input
that does not belong in the URL.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The envelope is the request; the letter inside is the
body.
R E A L E X A M P L E
POST /users body:
{"name":"Ada","email":"a@example.com"}.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
The request body contains payload data, typically JSON
or form data, for operations that create or modify
resources.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 012 / 310

013
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Query parameters
I N O N E B R E AT H
Key-value values appended to a URL after ? to alter
how a resource is retrieved. They are convenient for
filtering, sorting, searching, and pagination.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You order "pizza?size=large&spicy=true" instead of
inventing a new pizza endpoint.
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /products?
category=laptops&page=2&sort=price.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use query parameters for optional modifiers such as
filters, sort order, search terms, and pagination.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 013 / 310

014
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Path parameter
I N O N E B R E AT H
A dynamic segment in a URL path used to identify a
specific resource or nested location. It gives stable,
readable resource addresses.
M A K E I T S T I C K
/dogs/fluffy means "the dog named Fluffy", not "all
dogs with ?dog=fluffy".
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /users/42 where 42 is the user ID.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Path parameters usually identify a concrete resource,
while query parameters usually modify how a collection
is retrieved.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 014 / 310

015
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
REST API
I N O N E B R E AT H
An API style centered on resources, standard HTTP
semantics, stateless requests, and representations. It
gives teams a predictable way to design web APIs.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A library has /books/42, not /
pleaseGiveMeBookNumber42Now.
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /users/42, PATCH /users/42, DELETE /users/
42.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
REST models resources and uses HTTP semantics
consistently. I focus more on clear resource contracts
than on blindly following naming rules.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 015 / 310

016
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
API
I N O N E B R E AT H
A defined interface through which software
components communicate. It separates
implementation details from the contract consumers
rely on.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A vending machine exposes buttons and a coin slot;
you do not need to know its internal gears.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Frontend calls /api/orders; a payment service
exposes a create-payment API.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An API is a contract between software components.
Web APIs often use HTTP, but APIs can also be libraries,
OS interfaces, or messaging contracts.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 016 / 310

017
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
JSON
I N O N E B R E AT H
A lightweight text format for structured data using
objects, arrays, strings, numbers, booleans, and null.
It is easy for humans to read and common across web
APIs.
M A K E I T S T I C K
JSON is a lunchbox with labeled compartments:
name, age, skills.
R E A L E X A M P L E
{"name":"Ada","skills":["JS","React"]}.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
JSON is a language-neutral text representation
commonly used for API payloads; in JavaScript I
serialize with JSON.stringify and parse with JSON.parse.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 017 / 310

018
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Serialization
I N O N E B R E AT H
Converting in-memory data into a transport or storage
representation; deserialization reverses it. Processes
cannot directly send a JavaScript object through a
network cable.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You flatten a LEGO castle into labeled bags for
shipping, then rebuild it at the destination.
R E A L E X A M P L E
JS object -> JSON string -> network -> parse
back into data.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Serialization turns runtime data into a portable
representation such as JSON; deserialization
reconstructs usable data from it.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 018 / 310

019
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
CORS
I N O N E B R E AT H
A browser-enforced policy that controls whether
frontend JavaScript can read responses from another
origin. It prevents arbitrary websites from freely reading
sensitive cross-origin responses.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A nightclub bouncer checks whether website A is on
website B's guest list.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Frontend http://localhost:5173 calls API http://
localhost:8000; server returns Access-Control-
Allow-Origin.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
CORS is a browser security mechanism based on server
response headers. It is not authentication and it does not
stop non-browser clients.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 019 / 310

020
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Origin
I N O N E B R E AT H
The browser security identity formed by scheme,
host, and port. Same-origin rules use it to decide which
resources can interact freely.
M A K E I T S T I C K
https://cat.com:443 and http://cat.com:80 are
cousins, not twins.
R E A L E X A M P L E
https://example.com differs from https://
api.example.com and https://example.com:8080.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An origin is scheme + host + port. A change in any of
those creates a different origin for browser security
purposes.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 020 / 310

021
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Proxy
I N O N E B R E AT H
An intermediary that forwards traffic between a client
and another service. It can centralize routing, policy,
caching, security, and protocol translation.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You tell a receptionist what you need; the
receptionist talks to the mysterious office behind the
wall.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Vite proxies /api to localhost:8000 during
development.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A proxy sits between two parties and forwards requests.
Depending on direction it can represent the client or the
servers behind it.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 021 / 310

022
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Reverse proxy
I N O N E B R E AT H
A proxy that sits in front of backend servers and
receives client traffic on their behalf. It hides internal
topology and can terminate TLS, route, cache, rate-
limit, and load balance.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The hotel front desk chooses which staff member
handles your request; guests never call room 412
directly.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Nginx receives api.example.com and forwards /
auth to one service and /orders to another.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A reverse proxy is the public entry point in front of
servers. I use it for routing, TLS termination, load
balancing, caching, and security controls.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 022 / 310

023
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
CDN
I N O N E B R E AT H
A geographically distributed edge network that serves
content close to users, often from cache. It lowers
latency and reduces load on the origin.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Instead of shipping every sandwich from Berlin to
Tokyo, you keep sandwiches in a Tokyo fridge.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Static JS, CSS, images, and fonts are served
from nearby edge locations.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A CDN reduces latency and origin traffic by serving
cacheable content from geographically distributed edge
nodes; modern CDNs also proxy dynamic traffic.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 023 / 310

024
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Cache
I N O N E B R E AT H
A faster storage layer that keeps reusable results so
expensive work can be avoided. It can reduce latency,
database load, API cost, and computation.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You leave your keys by the door instead of searching
the whole house every morning.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Check Redis for user:42; on miss, query Postgres
and store the result.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Caching trades freshness and complexity for speed. I
always think about key design, invalidation, TTLs, and
what happens on misses.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 024 / 310

025
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Cache hit
I N O N E B R E AT H
A cache lookup that finds a usable stored value. Hits
are where the latency and load savings come from.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You check the snack drawer and the cookie is
actually there. Victory.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Redis GET user:42 returns data, so no database
query is needed.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A cache hit means the requested item is available and
valid in cache, so the slower backing store can be
skipped.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 025 / 310

026
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
Cache miss
I N O N E B R E AT H
A lookup where the requested value is absent or
expired. The system must fall back to the source of
truth and often repopulate cache.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You open the snack drawer: empty. Now you must
walk to the supermarket.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Redis misses -> query DB -> return result ->
SETEX cache key.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
On a cache miss I fetch from the authoritative source
and usually populate the cache, while avoiding
stampedes under heavy concurrency.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Mid-level move: explain one trade-off, failure mode, or reason
you would choose a different tool.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 026 / 310

027
W E B , N E T WO R K I N G & D E L I V E RY
TTL
I N O N E B R E AT H
Time To Live: how long a cached or leased value
remains valid before expiring. It bounds staleness and
prevents data from living forever.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A carton says "good for 60 seconds"; after that,

R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E

You text a friend directions from last Tuesday while
the restaurant moved yesterday.

setInterval(() => console.log(count),1000)
inside an effect with the wrong dependencies.

Functional state updates and refs solve some cases, but not

213
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Async request race
I N O N E B R E AT H
Two requests overlap and an older response arrives
after a newer one, overwriting fresh UI. Fast typing,
route changes, and filters can create incorrect data
even when every request succeeds.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You ask “weather Berlin?” then “weather Rome?”;

query A starts, query B starts, B returns, A

“Last response wins” is not always “latest intent wins.”
Explain it aloud before swiping. 213 / 310

214
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Component composition
I N O N E B R E AT H
Build larger UI by combining focused components
instead of adding endless configuration flags to one
component. It keeps APIs flexible and reduces giant
conditional components.

<Dialog><Dialog.Title/><Dialog.Body/></Dialog>

I prefer composition when consumers need flexible
structure; it often scales better than a component with
dozens of boolean props.

Too many tiny wrappers can also obscure the UI; use
meaningful boundaries.

215
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Headless component
I N O N E B R E AT H
Reusable behavior and accessibility without
prescribing final visual styling. It separates interaction
logic from product-specific appearance.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You buy the engine and steering system, then design
your own car body.
R E A L E X A M P L E
A headless combobox provides keyboard/focus
behavior; your design system supplies visuals.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Headless components are useful when teams need
robust behavior and accessibility with custom

216
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Compound component
I N O N E B R E AT H
A family of components designed to work together
through shared context or structure. It creates
expressive APIs for complex widgets.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A sandwich set gives you Bread, Filling, and Sauce
pieces that understand the same lunch.
R E A L E X A M P L E
<Tabs><Tabs.List/><Tabs.Panel/></Tabs>
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Compound components expose coordinated

Ensure hidden context does not make behavior mysterious.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 216 / 310

217
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Portal
I N O N E B R E AT H
Render a React subtree into a different DOM container
while keeping it in the same React tree. Useful for
overlays that must escape clipping or stacking contexts.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The actor belongs to Scene A but enters through a
trapdoor on a different part of the physical stage.
R E A L E X A M P L E
createPortal(<Dialog/>, document.body)
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Portals solve DOM placement issues for modals and
tooltips while preserving React context and event
semantics.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Portals do not magically solve accessibility, focus
management, or z-index architecture.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 217 / 310

218
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Suspense
I N O N E B R E AT H
A React mechanism for showing fallback UI while a
compatible child is not ready. It coordinates loading
boundaries and streaming experiences.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A theater closes one small curtain while changing
that set instead of blacking out the entire building.
R E A L E X A M P L E
<Suspense fallback={<Skeleton/>}><LazyPanel/></
Suspense>
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Suspense defines a loading boundary for compatible
asynchronous resources or lazy components.

Suspense.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 218 / 310

219
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Transition
I N O N E B R E AT H
A lower-priority React update that can be interrupted
so urgent interactions stay responsive. It helps
expensive non-urgent UI updates avoid blocking typing/
click feedback.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The cashier serves the person at the desk before
reorganizing the entire cereal aisle.
R E A L E X A M P L E
startTransition(()=>setFilter(next));
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Transitions mark updates as non-urgent so React can
prioritize immediate interactions and keep the interface
responsive.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A transition does not make expensive computation free; profile
real bottlenecks.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 219 / 310

220
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
useDeferredValue
I N O N E B R E AT H
Lets a derived part of UI lag behind an urgent value
temporarily. It keeps input responsive when
downstream rendering is expensive.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Your mouth says the new word instantly; the giant
scoreboard updates a moment later.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const deferredQuery = useDeferredValue(query);
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
useDeferredValue lets non-urgent rendering trail an
urgent value, which can improve responsiveness for
expensive result views.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Debouncing changes when work begins; deferring changes
rendering priority - not the same thing.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 220 / 310

221
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Memoization boundary
I N O N E B R E AT H
A deliberate place where stable inputs can allow
expensive work or child rendering to be reused. It can
reduce repeated computation, but adds complexity and
comparison overhead.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You laminate a frequently used map instead of
redrawing Europe every time someone asks where
France is.
R E A L E X A M P L E
React.memo(Chart), useMemo(expensiveProjection)
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I memoize after identifying a meaningful cost and stable
inputs, rather than wrapping every function and
component by habit.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Incorrect dependencies can create stale results; unnecessary
memoization can make code worse.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 221 / 310

222
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Referential stability
I N O N E B R E AT H
Whether the same object/function reference is
preserved across renders. React memoization and
effect dependencies often use reference identity.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Two identical-looking hotel keys are still different
physical keys.
R E A L E X A M P L E
const options = useMemo(()=>({limit:20}),[]);
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Referential stability matters when consumers compare
by identity, such as memoized children or effect
dependencies.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not stabilize references unless identity actually matters.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 222 / 310

223
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
State machine
I N O N E B R E AT H
An explicit model of allowed states and transitions. It
prevents impossible UI combinations in complex flows.
M A K E I T S T I C K
An elevator can be MOVING or DOOR_OPEN, but it
should not be both.
R E A L E X A M P L E
idle -> submitting -> success | error
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
For complex flows I model explicit states and transitions
instead of independent booleans whose combinations
can become invalid.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A full state-machine library is optional; the mental model itself
is valuable.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 223 / 310

224
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Render purity
I N O N E B R E AT H
A React render should calculate UI from inputs without
causing external side effects. Pure rendering lets
React safely rerun, pause, or discard work.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A restaurant menu printer may print the menu twice;
it must not charge your card each time it prints.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Do not call fetch-and-write or localStorage
mutation directly during render.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
React rendering should be pure: same props/state/
context should describe the same UI without external
mutations.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Development behaviors may intentionally render more than
once to expose impurity.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 224 / 310

225
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Strict Mode
I N O N E B R E AT H
A development tool that enables checks and
intentionally stresses some lifecycle assumptions. It
exposes unsafe side effects and cleanup mistakes
earlier.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The driving instructor makes you repeat the
maneuver to see whether your car only works by
luck.
R E A L E X A M P L E
<StrictMode><App/></StrictMode>
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Strict Mode adds development-only checks; apparent
duplicate execution can reveal effects that are not
idempotent or correctly cleaned up.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not “fix” Strict Mode by disabling it before understanding
the bug.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 225 / 310

226
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Error recovery boundary
I N O N E B R E AT H
A UI boundary designed not just to show an error but
to offer a meaningful recovery path. Production UX
should degrade locally rather than turning the whole
page into a dead end.
M A K E I T S T I C K
If the toaster breaks, you replace breakfast - you do
not evacuate the entire house.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Widget error -> retry button; editor error ->
preserve draft and reload component.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I place error boundaries around meaningful failure
domains and design recovery, telemetry, and preserved
user work where possible.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
An error boundary does not catch every async/event-handler
error automatically.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 226 / 310

227
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Feature boundary
I N O N E B R E AT H
A module/component boundary aligned with a user-
facing capability rather than file type alone. It
improves ownership and keeps related UI, hooks, tests,
and data logic close.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Keep everything for “pizza delivery” in one kitchen
station instead of putting every spoon in one building
and every plate in another.
R E A L E X A M P L E
features/search/{SearchBox, useSearch, api,
tests}
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Feature-oriented boundaries often scale better than
giant global folders like components/, hooks/, utils/
when product complexity grows.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Shared primitives should remain genuinely shared, not become
a dumping ground.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 227 / 310

228
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Presentational vs
orchestration logic
I N O N E B R E AT H
Separate UI rendering from workflow/data
coordination when that separation clarifies
responsibilities. It makes complex screens easier to
test and redesign.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The waiter handles the table; the kitchen coordinates
cooking. One person can do both in a tiny cafe, but
not always at scale.
R E A L E X A M P L E
SearchPage orchestrates query/state; ResultsList
renders rows.

reduces coupling, while avoiding rigid “container/
component” ceremony for simple cases.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
The boundary is a tool, not a mandatory folder pattern.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 228 / 310

229
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Optimistic concurrency in
UI

Allow local interaction immediately, then reconcile
with authoritative server state and version/conflict
rules. It makes collaborative or latency-sensitive UIs
feel fast without pretending conflicts cannot happen.

You pencil your name into the booking sheet, then
the receptionist confirms whether someone else
took the slot first.

Update UI -> send mutation with version ->
accept or rollback/conflict message.

concurrency guarantees and a clear rollback/conflict
strategy.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A pretty optimistic animation cannot fix duplicate writes or lost
updates on the server.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 229 / 310

230
R E AC T: S TAT E , I D E N T I T Y & A R C H I T E C T U R E
Accessibility state
I N O N E B R E AT H
Interactive components must expose their current
state to assistive technologies, not only visually. A
screen reader needs to know expanded, selected,

A traffic light that changes color but never tells a

native disabled

Prefer native controls because they carry much of this
behavior automatically.

231
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Module
I N O N E B R E AT H
A cohesive unit that exposes a public interface while
hiding internal implementation details. Modules
reduce the amount of code a developer must
understand at once.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A microwave has buttons on the front; you do not
need its wiring diagram to heat soup.
R E A L E X A M P L E
payments/index.ts exports charge(); internal
gateway mapping stays private.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
A good module has a focused responsibility, a small
public surface, and internals that can change without
breaking callers.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
A folder is not automatically a module; the dependency
boundary matters.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 231 / 310

232
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Encapsulation
I N O N E B R E AT H
Hide internal state/implementation and expose only
the operations consumers need. It prevents distant
code from depending on fragile details.
M A K E I T S T I C K
You drive using steering wheel and pedals, not by
reaching into the gearbox with your hand.
R E A L E X A M P L E

cart.items internals directly.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Encapsulation protects invariants by controlling how
state and behavior are accessed.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Getters for every private field are not meaningful encapsulation
if callers still control everything.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 232 / 310

233
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Abstraction
I N O N E B R E AT H
A simplified model/interface that hides irrelevant
detail for a particular task. It lets callers reason at the
right level.
M A K E I T S T I C K
“Send message” is useful; “open TCP socket,
serialize bytes, retry packet 17…” is too low-level for
most callers.
R E A L E X A M P L E

is IndexedDB or remote.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
An abstraction should hide volatility and expose the
concepts consumers actually care about.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Bad abstractions hide important differences or force every
implementation into the wrong shape.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 233 / 310

234
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Contract
I N O N E B R E AT H
The behavior, inputs, outputs, errors, and guarantees
that callers may rely on. Stable contracts let
implementations evolve independently.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A restaurant promises “order before 10, receive
food”; it does not promise which chef uses which
pan.
R E A L E X A M P L E
GET /users/:id returns User or 404 with
documented schema.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I design module/API contracts around observable
behavior and keep implementation details out of the
public surface.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Version or migrate breaking contract changes deliberately.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 234 / 310

235
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Dependency inversion
I N O N E B R E AT H
High-level business logic depends on abstractions/
capabilities rather than concrete infrastructure
details. It reduces coupling to databases, vendors, and
frameworks.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The lamp depends on “electricity from a socket,” not
“this exact power station turbine #7.”
R E A L E X A M P L E
CheckoutService accepts PaymentGateway
interface; Stripe adapter implements it.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Dependency inversion keeps domain policy independent
from replaceable infrastructure by depending on stable
interfaces.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Do not invent interfaces for every class; use them where
volatility or testing justifies the seam.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 235 / 310

236
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Ports and adapters
I N O N E B R E AT H
Architecture where core logic exposes/consumes
ports and external systems connect through adapters.
It keeps domain behavior testable and independent
from UI/database/vendor details.
M A K E I T S T I C K
The castle has standardized gates; horses, cars, and
delivery robots can each use an adapter to enter.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Domain -> PaymentPort; StripePaymentAdapter ->
Stripe SDK.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Ports-and-adapters isolates core use cases from
infrastructure and makes external integrations
replaceable.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Useful when domain logic matters; excessive ceremony is
wasteful for tiny CRUD apps.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 236 / 310

237
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Layered architecture
I N O N E B R E AT H
Organize responsibilities into layers such as
presentation, application, domain, and infrastructure.
It creates dependency direction and reduces cross-
cutting spaghetti.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Guests talk to the waiter, waiter to kitchen; guests do
not sprint into the freezer.
R E A L E X A M P L E
UI -> service/use case -> repository ->
database.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Layering is useful when each layer has a clear
responsibility and dependencies mostly flow inward/
downward.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Avoid pass-through layers that add files but no semantic value.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 237 / 310

238
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Pure core, imperative
shell
I N O N E B R E AT H
Keep business rules pure where possible and put I/O/
side effects at the edges. It makes critical logic
deterministic and easy to test.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Do the math on paper first; only then call the bank,
printer, and email robot.
R E A L E X A M P L E
calculateQuote(input) is pure; handler fetches
DB data and sends result.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I isolate side effects at boundaries and keep core
decision logic pure when practical.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Not every application needs a perfectly pure domain; optimize
for clarity.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 238 / 310

239
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Single Responsibility
Principle
I N O N E B R E AT H
A module should have one coherent reason to change.
It prevents unrelated concerns from becoming
entangled.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A Swiss Army knife is useful; a Swiss Army
refrigerator-toaster-tax-accountant is not.
R E A L E X A M P L E
InvoiceCalculator calculates totals; EmailSender
sends invoices.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
SRP is about reasons to change, not making every
function microscopic.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
Over-splitting can create navigation overhead and weak
abstractions.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 239 / 310

240
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Open/Closed Principle
I N O N E B R E AT H
Prefer designs that allow new behavior through
extension without repeatedly modifying fragile central
logic. It can reduce regression risk in frequently
extended systems.
M A K E I T S T I C K
Add a new train carriage instead of welding a new
room into the locomotive engine each week.
R E A L E X A M P L E
Renderer registry maps type -> renderer instead
of a 500-line switch edited by every feature.
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
I use extension points where variation is proven and
frequent; I do not pre-build plugin systems for
hypothetical needs.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
YAGNI still applies.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 240 / 310

241
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Adapter pattern
I N O N E B R E AT H
Wrap an incompatible or vendor-specific interface
behind the interface your application wants. It
contains third-party churn and translation logic.
M A K E I T S T I C K
A travel plug lets your German charger work in a UK
socket without rebuilding the laptop.
R E A L E X A M P L E
AnalyticsAdapter.track(event) wraps
VendorSDK.sendWeirdPayload(...).
S AY T H I S I N T H E I N T E R V I E W
Adapters translate between boundaries and keep
vendor-specific details from leaking through the
codebase.
WAT C H / L E V E L- U P
An adapter should simplify the boundary, not merely rename
every method one-to-one.
Explain it aloud before swiping. 241 / 310

242
M O D U L A R I T Y & M A I N TA I N A B I L I T Y
Repository pattern
I N O N E B R E AT H
An abstraction representing access to domain data

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N

How much can two accountants see of each other's

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N

DATA B AS E S I N P R O D U C T I O N

only whiteboard.

batches to durable store.

acceptable.

I N O N E B R E AT H

entry when space is needed. It exploits temporal
locality: recently used items are often reused soon.

when a new mug arrives.

exists.

WAT C H / L E V E L- U P

risk.

I N O N E B R E AT H

A I E N G I N E E R I N G & L L M S Y S T E M S

I N O N E B R E AT H
Untrusted content attempts to manipulate model

attacker-controlled text from users, webpages, emails,

boundary.

malicious input.

Tool calling
I N O N E B R E AT H
A model selects a structured tool/function and

blindly.

I N O N E B R E AT H

schema such as JSON fields/enums. It makes AI

Schema-valid does not mean semantically correct.

Agent loop
I N O N E B R E AT H
A repeated cycle where a model observes state,
chooses an action/tool, receives results, and
continues until done. It supports multi-step tasks that
require planning and external operations.

→ check result.

-> final.

workflow that works.

I N O N E B R E AT H

latency, availability, or cost. Not every request needs
the largest model.

token selection. It changes diversity, not the model's
underlying knowledge.

low for constrained factual tasks and only raise it when
diversity is useful.

Temperature is not a “creativity intelligence” knob and cannot
fix poor grounding.

responsiveness in streaming AI UIs.

long until the whole speech ends.

Long prompts and queueing can dominate TTFT.

generation begins. It measures streaming generation
throughput perceived by the user.

the train moves once it arrives.

conditions.

for previously processed tokens so they do not need

efficient.

rereading the entire book before writing every next

reuses prior states.

response caching.

Reuse computation or results for identical/repeated

painful.

'nonce-...'

inject unsafe HTML.

their current job. It limits blast radius if credentials or

JavaScript Deep Dive
Know the return shape
Choosing an array method starts with the shape you
need back. One item, a new array and a yes-or-no
answer are different results.
items.find(test); // item or undefined
items.filter(test); // array
items.some(test); // boolean
items.every(test); // boolean
Find selects the first matching value. Filter creates an
array containing matching values. Some asks whether
a match exists; every asks whether all visited items
pass.
A boolean cannot be followed by .map(). Check the
return value before chaining methods.

SHELF SAMPLES / 02
Return is not decoration
With an arrow function, an expression body returns its
expression. A block body needs an explicit return
statement.
const a = [1, 2].map(n => n * 2);
// [2, 4]
const b = [1, 2].map(n => { n * 2; });
// [undefined, undefined]
The multiplication in the second example happens,
but its value is not returned by the callback. Map
collects the callback results.

Change a value, keep the original
To update an item without mutating the source array,
create a new array and a new object for the item that
changes.
const updated = games.map(game =>
game.title === "Eclipse"
? { ...game, favorite: true }
: game
);
Unchanged objects are reused here. This is a shallow
update, not a deep clone of every nested object.
